results.title: Tariffs send shockwaves through Georgia's industries
results.content:
In 2024, the Peach State ranked seventh nationwide in net exports, shipping around $53.1 billion in locally made products overseas while importing about $145.6 billion, according to the Georgia Chamber of Commerce.

President Donald Trump’s newly unveiled tariffs have sent shockwaves through the manufacturing, technology and agricultural sectors across the country — particularly in Georgia. [...] The White House initially established 10% tariffs on imports from all countries, along with higher “reciprocal” tariffs targeting nations such as China, Vietnam and members of the European Union that levy tariffs on U.S. goods. Mexico and Canada — Georgia’s top export destinations — were spared from the new tariffs. [...] Drew Echols, a fifth-generation peach farmer and state senator from Gainesville, said he feels optimistic about the prospect of tariffs creating headwinds for local crops and incentivizing more manufacturers to set up shop in Georgia after relocating their operations overseas.

“It’ll hurt in the short term — there’s no question,” Echols told _State Affairs_. “I’ve just got to hope that most of those companies come back.”

results.title: Trump's tariff plan sparks economic uncertainty in Georgia | FOX 5 Atlanta
results.content:
## Key Georgia Impacts by Sector

Local perspective:

#### Automotive

 Imported vehicle parts will face a 25% tariff, potentially raising production costs at Georgia’s auto plants.
 Export risks are rising, as global buyers may retaliate — particularly affecting the Port of Brunswick, the busiest auto port in the U.S.
 Uncertainty around USMCA exemptions adds confusion for manufacturers reliant on cross-border supply chains.

#### Construction and Manufacturing [...] The Port of Savannah and Port of Brunswick may see swings in cargo volumes as importers rush to beat deadlines, then scale back.
 Warehouse and transport operators face uncertainty as businesses reconfigure supply chains, stockpile goods, or shift sourcing strategies.
 While infrastructure investments are helping the ports remain resilient, retaliatory tariffs on U.S. exports could slow growth long term. [...] ATLANTA - As President Donald Trump’s sweeping new tariff measures roll out, Georgia businesses are preparing for ripple effects that could disrupt nearly every corner of the state’s economy. A baseline 10% tariff on imports took effect last week, with broader and steeper tariffs set to begin Wednesday — part of a broader trade policy overhaul that is being met with both praise and alarm.

 First sale rule: Pay duties based on the manufacturer or middleman price (rather than the importer price).

## Watch Our Tariff Talk Webinar [...] Reshoring: Consider automation opportunities and domestic suppliers (including those who can expand their production).
